title: Prefund Deposits for Hosting Renewals — Harborline Customer Accounts
content:
# Prefund deposits for hosting renewals

This policy sets the amount of the prefund deposit a holder makes so that account credit can pay, in the coming days, the charges that keep the website on their hosting plan running, each priced as its own product's published rules price that charge, whichever source pays it. The deposit is the holder's own money placed on their own account credit; account credit then pays those auto-renew charges when they come due.

## Conditions of any deposit

A deposit may be accepted only while the account status is active, a single deposit must be at least the tier's minimum deposit and at most the tier's maximum per transaction and must use one of the tier's deposit methods, a bank transfer must be at least the tier's bank transfer minimum, and a deposit that would raise the credit balance above the tier's maximum credit balance is refused in full, never accepted in part.

## When the prefund deposit is fixed

The prefund deposit is fixed only after the credit ledger carries a goodwill entry for the hosting plan of the customer's most recent initial-term charge whenever that plan, active and in its first term, was activated two or more calendar days after its order date and the account's goodwill entries dated after the same calendar date one year before today total less than the tier's yearly goodwill limit.

The prefund deposit is not fixed until the credit ledger carries a goodwill entry for the account's most recent approved recovery request whenever that request was decided more than seven calendar days after it was submitted and the account's goodwill entries dated after the same calendar date one year before today total less than the tier's yearly goodwill limit.

Before the prefund deposit is worked out, the credit ledger must carry a goodwill entry for the most recently refunded domain auto-renew charge whenever no other domain auto-renew refund line shares its refund date, the refunded charge had a same-day twin auto-renew charge of the same domain, and the account's goodwill entries dated after the same calendar date one year before today total less than the tier's yearly goodwill limit.

## The deposit is the holder's own payment

The prefund deposit is the account holder's own payment of money into their own Harborline account credit from one of their own payment methods: their card, their PayPal account or their bank transfer. The agent unlocks the customer-side tool `make_prefund_deposit_8453f2b2` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it. One run records one deposit: the payment is taken from the holder's chosen method, the account credit balance goes up by the amount deposited, and the deposit is recorded on the account's credit history with its funding method. The holder sees the deposit and the higher balance at once, and the credit is available for any Harborline charge, including auto-renewals that try account credit.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `account_id` | The reference number of the holder's Harborline account, as shown on the account record opened for this customer. | Identifier, as shown on the record |
| `funding_method` | How the holder pays the deposit. | One of `card` (charged to the holder's payment card), `paypal` (paid from the holder's PayPal account), `bank_transfer` (arrives by the holder's bank transfer); `none` is not a funding method for a deposit and is never the value for this tool |
| `amount` | The amount deposited, in US dollars. | A positive figure with 2 decimal places; any further decimals are rounded half up to the cent |

## Receipt and errors

A completed run returns a line beginning "Deposit recorded", stating the reference number of the new deposit entry, the amount deposited in US dollars with two decimals, the funding method used and the account's new credit balance in US dollars with two decimals. The run is refused with an error line when `amount` is not a positive US dollar figure, or when `funding_method` is not `card`, `paypal` or `bank_transfer`.

*Applies to: Harborline Customer Accounts*
